preamble.summary:
Add `phax plans estimate <plan> [--json] [--no-probe]`. It reports, before a run, what a plan will cost in API-list dollars (P10/P50/P90 per phase and for the run), calibrated from this machine's cost ledgers. It also says whether the plan fits the subscription windows left now (`fits`, `risky`, `wait`) or why it cannot say. The command reads the plan with the deterministic parser `phax plans lint` uses and never invokes a model. Without `--no-probe` it reads both windows from the OAuth usage endpoint. With `--no-probe` it uses the last rate-limit sample in the ledgers. It exits 0 whatever the verdict, and 12 when the plan fails artifact validation.

The work depends on the `cost-ledger` spec, which has landed: `<run folder>/cost-ledger.json` for kept runs (`src/schemas/costLedger.ts`), copies at `<state root>/cost-ledgers/<namespace>.<short-name>.<run-id>.json` for pruned runs, and `phax cost backfill`. The reference behaviour is the spike `spikes/plan-estimate/phax_estimate.py` (`features`, `training_set`, `fit`, `reprice`, `calibrate`, `play`). Port its model, not its stream scan: the ledger already holds each invocation's own cost, tokens per model, `agentMs`, `endedAt` and rate-limit samples carrying `runCostUsd`. List prices come from `src/domain/routing/prices.ts` (`CLAUDE_LIST_PRICES`, `listPriceFor`). Add no `price` field to providers.json.

The report is one domain value, `EstimateReport`. `--json` prints it as is, and the text view renders it. Its shape is binding on every phase:

- `history`: `{ phases, required: 60, halfLifeDays: 30, unledgeredRuns }`. `phases` is the number of sized historical phases the fit used. `unledgeredRuns` is the number of kept runs that have no `cost-ledger.json` yet, so the view can suggest `phax cost backfill`.
- `phases`: one entry per plan phase, as a discriminated union. An estimated phase is `{ id, provider, model, effort, estimate: { p10, p50, p90 } }`. A phase that is not estimated is `{ id, provider, model, effort, estimate: null, notEstimated: "other-provider" | "no-list-price" }`. `model` is the concrete model routing selects for the phase. The list is empty when history is thin.
- `run`: `{ p10, p50, p90, runLevel }`, or `null` when history is thin.
- `notEstimated`: always `plan-extraction`, `plan-auditor` and `interactive-code-review`. It adds `compliance-review` when the compliance review is enabled but cannot be estimated (routed to another provider, or no compliance entry in history).
- `windows`: `{ source: "oauth-usage" | "last-sample", observedAt, fiveHour: { utilization, resetsAt, capacityUsd }, sevenDay: { … } }`, or `null`. `capacityUsd` is a number, or `null` when that window is uncalibrated.
- `windowsUnavailable`: the reason string when the verdict is `windows-unavailable`, else `null`.
- `burnRateUsdPerHour`: a number, or `null`.
- `verdict`: `fits` | `risky` | `wait` | `no-subscription` | `windows-unavailable`, plus the variants Q1 decides (recommended: `thin-history` and `uncalibrated`).
- `uncalibrated`: the list of `five-hour` | `seven-day` | `burn-rate` that could not be calibrated; empty otherwise.
- `scenarios`: `{ p50: { pauses, endsAt }, p90: { pauses, endsAt } }`, or `null`. Each pause is `{ phase, window: "five-hour" | "seven-day", at, resumesAt }`.
- `warnings`: an array of strings.

Dollar amounts are rounded to 2 decimals. Instants are ISO-8601 UTC.

The verdict is decided in this order. History under 60 sized phases gives `thin-history`, with no estimate. Otherwise there is an estimate, and then the first of `no-subscription`, `windows-unavailable` or `uncalibrated` that applies. Only when none applies are both scenarios played forward and the verdict is `fits`, `risky` or `wait`.

Test hygiene for every phase. Tests never spawn a provider, never call the network, never read `~/.phax`, `~/.claude` or the macOS Keychain. They use fake FileSystem/Git/credentials/endpoint adapters, temp directories and made-up ledgers. A test that spawns the CLI sets `HOME` to a temp dir and runs in its own temp git repo. It always passes either `--no-probe` or a dummy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so the credentials adapter short-circuits before any store is touched, including the Keychain, which `HOME` does not redirect. No fixture is copied from this repository's plans, specs, run folders or `~/.phax`. The spec's §6 numbers are made up and may be reused.
preamble.requiredCommandsNote: Phase-03 runs both commands to regenerate `phax.usage.kdl`, the CLI reference and the README's generated CLI section. Both are already in `security.agentCommands` in `phax.json`, so the plan requires no security configuration change.
technicalArbitrations: Prices: the list prices come from `src/domain/routing/prices.ts` (`listPriceFor`), which carries one entry for every shipped Claude model. That is how §10's "catalog prices on every Claude entry" is met. No `price` field is added to providers.json (binding brief decision, 2026-10-17). Loss accepted: §6's sketched catalog field does not ship.

Historical features: only the kept runs of this repository are sized, meaning registry entries whose namespace equals `phax.json`'s name. Each phase's model, effort and planned files come from the run folder's `phax-plan.json`. Planned-file bytes are git blob sizes at the last commit before the registry entry's `createdAt` (`git rev-list -1 --before`). There is no fallback to file counts. Every reachable ledger, from kept runs of every namespace and pruned copies alike, feeds the window calibration, the burn rate and the run-level median. Pruned runs contribute no features, and prune is not changed. Sizing every repository the registry reaches is not an option, because the registry records no repository path. Loss accepted: a new repository gets no estimate until it has 60 sized phases of its own, and the base commit is approximated from the start time.

Regression: the spike's model. Features are an intercept, effort indicators (medium, high, xhigh, max against a low baseline; `ultracode` counts as max and `none` as low), log1p(edit KB), log1p(optional KB) and log1p(files to create). The fit is weighted least squares with a 1e-6 ridge on log token volume priced at `claude-opus-5-5`, with a half-life of 30 days counted back from now. The prediction is repriced at the phase's model through the history's weighted token mix. The ledger keeps one `cacheWriteTokens` count, so cache writes are priced at the 1-hour write price, as in the spike's backtest. Loss accepted: cache writes Claude Code actually made at 5 minutes are overpriced in the token volume. The 1h/5m ratio is 1.6 for every catalog model, so the ratio between models is unchanged.

Quantiles: a phase's P10/P50/P90 are the exact weighted quantiles of the residuals applied to its base estimate, with no sampling. Two phases that differ only by model therefore differ exactly by the price ratio (§8). The run's quantiles come from 4,000 seeded draws (mulberry32, seed 7), with independent residuals per phase plus the run-level cost, so the output and the tests are reproducible. Loss accepted: the sum of the phase P50s is not the run P50.

A Claude model without a list price (one added to providers.json) is listed as not estimated (`no-list-price`). It is excluded from the run estimate and the verdict, exactly as §5.6 treats other providers, and it is never priced $0. Loss accepted: the run total and the verdict leave out a phase, which is named in the output.

Burn rate: the API-list cost over the agent hours of the `complete` ledger entries with `agentMs > 0`, in the 30 days ending at the newest such entry. Backfilled partial entries (`agentMs` 0) are excluded from both sums. When there is no such entry the burn rate is `null` and `burn-rate` is uncalibrated (see Q1). Loss accepted: gate time is not agent time, so a pause is predicted slightly early.

Window calibration: within one ledger, for one window, samples sharing a `resetsAt` form a group in entry order. A group needs at least two samples. It contributes Δcost (last `runCostUsd` minus first) and Δutilization (last minus first) and is dated by the `endedAt` of the entry holding its last sample. Groups dated in the 28 days before now with Δcost > 0 are kept, and capacity = 100 × ΣΔcost / ΣΔutilization. A window with ΣΔutilization = 0 is uncalibrated (see Q1), never a constant. Loss accepted: interactive use during a run inflates Δutilization, so capacity errs low, which leans towards pausing.

Run-level cost: when `review.compliance` is enabled and routing sends it to Claude Code, `runLevel` is the median, taken as the sorted value at index ⌊n/2⌋, of the per-ledger compliance costs whose last compliance entry ended in the 60 days before the newest one. In the forward play it is added to the last estimated phase. Loss accepted: a pause caused by the compliance review is attributed to the last phase.

Routing: each phase's provider and concrete model come from `resolveModel` with the security filter `phax run` uses for `config.security.profile`. Phase-02 extracts that filter as `securityFilterFor(policy)` and makes `executePlan` use it, so both paths decide the same way. A phase is estimated only when the selected provider is `claude-code`, and it is priced and shown at the selected concrete model.

Credentials: a non-empty `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` gives `no-subscription`, without reading any store. On macOS phax reads the Keychain item `Claude Code-credentials`; if the item is missing it falls back to `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude>/.credentials.json`. No store at all, or a store without `claudeAiOauth`, gives `no-subscription`. A store that exists but cannot be read or decoded gives `windows-unavailable` with a reason that never quotes its content. An expired `expiresAt` gives `windows-unavailable` ("start Claude Code to refresh it") without calling the endpoint, and phax never refreshes the token. A `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the environment with no store gives `windows-unavailable`, because phax does not read that variable. The token is decoded as an Effect `Redacted<string>` in infra. It travels through app only as a Redacted value and never enters the domain, an error message, a log, telemetry or a record. Loss accepted: macOS may ask once to allow phax to read the Keychain item.
No persisted format: the estimate writes nothing. `--json` is command output, so nothing is registered or snapshotted in `packages/schemas`.

Phase guard: `plans estimate` is classified `refused` inside a phase worktree. It writes nothing, but it reads the subscription credential and calls the network, and a phase has no use for either. Loss accepted: an agent cannot estimate a plan from inside a phase.

The §10 yardstick (run-level median error within ×1.35 on held-out runs) is checked by a unit test. The test generates a made-up history from a known log-linear model with seeded noise, holds out the most recent runs and asserts the median run-level error. On real history it is checked at review with the spike's `--exclude-run` backtest against the new command's output. No flag is added. Loss accepted: the gates never see real history.

Three phases: the pure domain, then the edges, then the surface. The credential and network code gets its own reviewable commit. Every commit stays green, because knip treats `src/app`, `src/infra` and the tests as entries.

openQuestions.question: How does the report give a verdict when it cannot compute one for a reason §6 does not list: fewer than 60 sized phases (§5.7), or a window or burn rate that cannot be calibrated from the last 28/30 days?

options.label: Add two verdict values, `thin-history` and `uncalibrated`, each with its reason (`history.phases`, and `uncalibrated: ["five-hour"|"seven-day"|"burn-rate"]`); windows are still read and shown
options.abandons: §6's five verdict values as the complete normative list: a script matching on five values meets two more

options.label: Keep the five values; a report that cannot decide carries `verdict: null` and a `verdictUnavailable` reason
options.abandons: a verdict string on every report: `jq .verdict` prints null and a script must read a second field to learn why

options.label: Fold both into `windows-unavailable` with the reason
options.abandons: windows-unavailable meaning the windows could not be read: a script cannot tell an endpoint failure from a history that is too thin

openQuestions.rationale: Explicit per-variant enums are the project rule. A names each case, and a script still reads one field. B reintroduces a nullable catch-all, and C misreports a calibration gap as an endpoint failure. The phases are written for A. If B or C is decided, the domain report's verdict union and its rendering follow the Decision block instead.

commit.subject: feat(cost): estimate a plan's cost and subscription fit from cost ledgers
commit.body:
Add the pure domain behind phax plans estimate, ported from the spike's model rather than its stream scan.

history.ts turns cost ledgers and sized run plans into training samples, and also computes the burn rate, the run-level compliance median, the window calibration from rate-limit sample groups and the last observed windows. fit.ts fits weighted least squares on log token volume priced at claude-opus-5-5 (half-life 30 days), reprices through the history's token mix, computes exact weighted residual quantiles per phase and seeded run draws. forecast.ts plays the phases forward through the five-hour and seven-day windows and gives fits, risky or wait. estimate.ts assembles the EstimateReport, including thin history, unpriced models, other providers and uncalibrated windows.

Unit tests on made-up ledgers cover each §8 criterion the domain owns, and a synthetic backtest holds the run-level median error within ×1.35.

phases.title: Estimate, calibration and forward play in the domain
phases.objective: phax can compute a plan's cost estimate and its subscription verdict as pure functions of made-up ledgers, sized run plans, plan phases and a window reading. The estimate is P10/P50/P90 per phase and per run. This phase adds no I/O and no surface.
detailedInstructions: Read `spikes/plan-estimate/phax_estimate.py` (`features`, `training_set`, `fit`, `solve`, `reprice`, `quantiles`, `calibrate`, `play`) and the preamble's Technical arbitrations and report shape before writing code. Port the model, not the stream scan. The input is `CostLedger` values (`src/schemas/costLedger.ts`), never streams.

`src/domain/cost/history.ts`. Define the input types. `LedgerSource = { runKey: string; ledger: CostLedger }`. `HistoricalPhasePlan = { id: string; model: string; effort: Effort; editBytes: number; optionalBytes: number; createCount: number }`. `SizedRun = { runKey: string; startedAt: string /* ISO */; phases: readonly HistoricalPhasePlan[] }`.

history.ts: `trainingSamples(ledgers, sizedRuns)` joins each sized run with the ledger of the same `runKey`. For each plan phase it sums the tokens per field (input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite) across all models, together with `costUsd`, over the ledger entries whose `phase` equals the phase id, roles phase/fix/handoff included. `y` is the log of that token volume priced at `REFERENCE_MODEL` (`claude-opus-5-5`, from `listPriceFor`) with the 1-hour cache-write price. Skip a phase whose reference-priced volume is under $0.01, which includes phases absent from the ledger such as ones that ran on Codex. A sample is `{ x: features(...), y, atMs: Date.parse(startedAt), tokens: [in, out, cacheRead, cacheWrite], costUsd }`.

history.ts: `burnRate(ledgers)` returns USD per agent hour, or `null`. It uses only `completeness: "complete"` entries with `agentMs > 0`, in the 30 days ending at the newest such entry's `endedAt`, as Σ costUsd / Σ agentMs·3.6e6. `runLevelMedian(ledgers)` returns USD or `null`. It sums each ledger's `role: "compliance"` entries (only ledgers that have at least one), keeps those whose last compliance `endedAt` lies in the 60 days before the newest compliance entry, sorts them and takes the value at index ⌊n/2⌋.

history.ts: `calibrateWindows(ledgers, nowMs)` returns `{ fiveHour: { capacityUsd: number | null; groups: number }, sevenDay: … }`. Per ledger and per window (`five-hour`, `seven-day`), walk the samples in entry order and group them by `resetsAt`. A group with at least 2 samples contributes Δcost = last.runCostUsd − first.runCostUsd and Δutil = last.utilization − first.utilization, dated by the `endedAt` of the entry holding its last sample. Keep groups dated in the 28 days before now with Δcost > 0. capacityUsd = 100·ΣΔcost/ΣΔutil, or `null` when ΣΔutil ≤ 0. Never return a constant.

history.ts: `lastObservedWindows(ledgers, nowMs)`. For each window, take the latest sample: the last sample of that window in the entry with the greatest `endedAt` that holds one. `observedAt` is that entry's `endedAt`. A window whose `resetsAt` is not after now becomes `{ utilization: 0, resetsAt: now + 5 h | 7 d }` (§5.9). Return `{ kind: "windows", source: "last-sample", observedAt /* the older of the two */, fiveHour, sevenDay }`, or `{ kind: "unavailable", reason: "no <window> sample in the ledgers" }` when a window has no sample.

`src/domain/cost/fit.ts`: constants `REFERENCE_MODEL`, `HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 30`, `MIN_HISTORY_PHASES = 60`, `RUN_DRAWS = 4000`, `RUN_SEED = 7`. `features(effort, editBytes, optionalBytes, createCount)` returns `[1, medium?, high?, xhigh?, max?, log1p(editBytes/1000), log1p(optionalBytes/1000), log1p(createCount)]`, where `ultracode` maps to max, and low, `none`, `off` and every other value are the baseline.

fit.ts: `fitCostModel(samples, nowMs)` weights each sample by 0.5^(max(0, nowMs − atMs)/86 400 000/30) and builds the weighted normal equations with +1e-6 on the diagonal. It solves them by Gauss–Jordan with partial pivoting, as the spike's `solve` does. It returns `{ beta, residuals, weights, mix }`, where `mix` is the weighted sum of the four token fields.

fit.ts: `repriceRatio(price, mix)` = Σ mix·[input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite1h] at `price` divided by the same sum at the reference price. `weightedQuantile(values, weights, q)` returns the smallest value, in sorted order, whose cumulative weight reaches q·Σw. `phaseQuantiles(model, x, price)` returns `{ base, p10, p50, p90 }` with base = exp(β·x)·repriceRatio and pq = base·exp(weightedQuantile(residuals, weights, q)).

fit.ts: `runQuantiles(model, bases, runLevelUsd)` uses a local mulberry32 PRNG seeded with `RUN_SEED`. Each of `RUN_DRAWS` draws picks, for every phase independently, one residual with probability proportional to its weight, and sums base·exp(r) plus `runLevelUsd`. Sort the draws and take v[min(n−1, ⌊q·n⌋)] for q = 0.1, 0.5 and 0.9. With no estimated phase, all three equal `runLevelUsd`.

`src/domain/cost/forecast.ts`: `playForward({ phaseCosts: [{ phase, usd }], burnUsdPerHour, fiveHour, sevenDay, capacity: { fiveHourUsd, sevenDayUsd }, nowMs })` returns `{ pauses: [{ phase, window, atMs, resumesAtMs }], endsAtMs }`. Port the spike's `play`. When t reaches a window's reset, the window opens at utilization 0 with a new reset at t + its duration. Room is max(0, 100 − u)·capacity/100 for each window. The step is the minimum of what is left, both rooms, and the burn until the five-hour reset. With zero room the run pauses until that window's reset. Both capacities must be positive numbers (callers guarantee it), so the loop always progresses. `verdictOf(p50, p90)` returns `fits` when P90 has no pause, `risky` when only P90 pauses, and `wait` when P50 pauses.

`src/domain/cost/estimate.ts`. Define the domain inputs. `PlanPhaseInput = { id, provider: ProviderId, model /* selected concrete model */, effort, editBytes, optionalBytes, createCount }`. `WindowsReading` is one of `{ kind: "windows", source: "oauth-usage" | "last-sample", observedAt, fiveHour: { utilization, resetsAt }, sevenDay }`, `{ kind: "no-subscription" }` or `{ kind: "unavailable", reason }`. `ComplianceInput` is one of `{ kind: "disabled" }`, `{ kind: "claude-code" }` or `{ kind: "other-provider" }`. Define `EstimateReport` exactly as the preamble describes, with the Q1 variants (recommended: `thin-history`, `uncalibrated`). Use explicit discriminated unions, not optional keys.

estimate.ts: `estimatePlan({ phases, ledgers, sizedRuns, unledgeredRuns, compliance, windows, nowMs })` builds the report. Fewer than `MIN_HISTORY_PHASES` training samples gives the `thin-history` report: `history.phases` set, `phases: []`, `run: null`, `scenarios: null`, windows passed through. Otherwise it fits. A phase whose provider is not `claude-code` is `notEstimated: "other-provider"`. A Claude phase whose `listPriceFor(model)` is undefined is `no-list-price`, never $0. An estimated phase gets its quantiles. `runLevel` comes from `runLevelMedian` only when compliance is `claude-code` and the median is not null. When compliance is enabled but not estimable, `compliance-review` is added to `notEstimated` and `runLevel` is 0.

estimate.ts verdict: thin-history first, then `no-subscription`, then `windows-unavailable` (set `windowsUnavailable` to the reason, `windows: null`), then `uncalibrated` (a window with a null capacity, or a null burn rate, each listed in `uncalibrated`). Otherwise build the P50 and P90 scenarios with `playForward`, using each estimated phase's P50 (or P90) in plan order with `runLevel` added to the last one, and set the verdict with `verdictOf`. Add a warning for each estimated phase whose effort column has fewer than 5 historical samples. Round dollars to 2 decimals and emit ISO instants.

`tests/helpers/costHistory.ts`: made-up builders for a `CostLedger` entry (role, phase, model, tokens, cost, agentMs, endedAt, samples), a ledger, a `SizedRun`, and a seeded history generator that produces N runs of k phases from a known log-linear model. Phase-02 reuses it. Every value is invented.
Tests use made-up data only, and no test reads a file outside the repository's test helpers.
phases.boundaryContracts: Producer: `src/domain/cost/estimate.ts` exports `estimatePlan`, the input types (`LedgerSource`, `SizedRun`, `HistoricalPhasePlan`, `PlanPhaseInput`, `WindowsReading`, `ComplianceInput`) and `EstimateReport`. `src/domain/cost/history.ts` exports `lastObservedWindows`, which builds the `--no-probe` reading. Consumers, in phase-02: the app use case gathers ledgers, sized runs, the resolved phases and a `WindowsReading`, and passes them in unchanged. In phase-03, the renderer and `--json` print `EstimateReport` as is. The domain never receives a credential and never computes a time zone. `nowMs` comes in from outside.
phases.testStrategy: Write the unit tests first, against made-up ledgers built with `tests/helpers/costHistory.ts`. `fit.test.ts`: WLS recovers known coefficients on noiseless data. Weights halve every 30 days. `weightedQuantile` is ordered and correct on small hand-checked arrays. Two phases identical but for model have P50s in exactly the opus-5-5/sonnet-5-5 repricing ratio for the history's mix (§8 priced at its own model). A larger edit size gives a larger P50 (§8 bigger files). History whose recent phases cost twice the older ones gives a P50 closer to the recent cost (§8 recent runs). Run quantiles are reproducible across calls and ordered P10 ≤ P50 ≤ P90. `history.test.ts`: phase aggregation across phase/fix/handoff roles and models. Calibration of $40 per 100 % in the last 28 days against $18 older gives capacityUsd 40 (§8 capacity). Groups need two samples and the same `resetsAt`. A window with no usable group gives null. The burn rate ignores partial entries with agentMs 0. The run-level median covers both the recent window and the null case. In `lastObservedWindows`, a passed reset gives utilization 0, and the age comes from `endedAt` (§8 --no-probe). `forecast.test.ts`: $31 left in the five-hour window with P50 $27 and P90 $39 gives risky, with the P90 pause naming the phase, `five-hour` and the reset instant. P90 under $31 gives fits. P50 over $31 gives wait (§8 verdicts). A seven-day exhaustion pauses until the seven-day reset. `estimate.test.ts`: 400 phases and a four-phase plan give ordered ranges (§8 ranges). 12 phases give thin-history, naming 12 (§8 thin history). A codex-cli phase is listed and excluded from the run and the verdict (§8 other providers). An unpriced Claude model is `no-list-price`. Compliance enabled gives `run.runLevel` equal to the recent median and includes it in the run (§8 run-level). no-subscription and windows-unavailable keep the estimate and set `windows: null` where required. A null capacity or burn rate gives `uncalibrated`. `backtest.test.ts`: generate about 30 runs × 4 phases over 120 days from a known model with seeded log-normal noise (σ ≈ 0.35), fit without the 6 most recent runs, and assert that the median over the held-out runs of max(P50/actual, actual/P50) is ≤ 1.35 (§10 yardstick).
implementationOrder: Test helpers and the made-up history generator.
`fit.ts`: features, WLS, reprice, weighted quantile and seeded run draws, test first.
`history.ts`: training samples, burn rate, run-level median, calibration and last observed windows, test first.
`forecast.ts`: forward play and verdict, test first.
`estimate.ts`: report assembly and verdict precedence, test first, then the backtest test.
excludedScope: Reading registries, ledgers, `phax-plan.json` or git: phase-02.
The credential and OAuth usage endpoint ports, adapters and schema: phase-02.
Text rendering, the CLI command, docs, README and NEXT_STEPS: phase-03.
Any change to the cost-ledger format or to prune.
phases.expectedHandoff: List the exact exported names and signatures of `src/domain/cost/history.ts`, `fit.ts`, `forecast.ts` and `estimate.ts`, especially `estimatePlan`'s input type, `WindowsReading`, `ComplianceInput`, `EstimateReport` and `lastObservedWindows`. Give the verdict variants implemented (per Q1's decision) and the builders `tests/helpers/costHistory.ts` offers. Record the backtest's measured median error. Explain any deviation from the planned file lists.

commit.subject: feat(cost): read history, subscription windows and the plan for an estimate
commit.body:
Add the edges of phax plans estimate.

The history reader collects every reachable cost ledger: registered runs of every namespace, plus pruned copies under cost-ledgers/. It sizes this repository's kept runs from their phax-plan.json and from git blob sizes at the last commit before each run started, using new Git.commitBefore and Git.blobSizes.

Two new ports carry the subscription side effects. SubscriptionCredentials reads Claude Code's OAuth token: the macOS Keychain, then .credentials.json. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY means no subscription. OAuthUsage calls the OAuth usage endpoint. The token is an Effect Redacted from the schema decode onwards and never reaches the domain, an error, a log or a record. The endpoint's answer is decoded through a schema, and any other shape is windows-unavailable.

estimatePlanCost reads the plan with the deterministic parser (artifact validation for docs/plans/), sizes its planned files in the working tree, routes each phase as phax run does through the extracted securityFilterFor, and returns the EstimateReport. Its layer has no Backend and no Shell.

phases.title: History, credentials, OAuth usage and the estimate use case
phases.objective: An app use case, `estimatePlanCost`, produces the full `EstimateReport` for a plan on disk. It reads the cost ledgers and sized history through FileSystem and Git, and the current windows through two new ports: subscription credentials and the OAuth usage endpoint. The OAuth token never leaves infra and app, and only as a Redacted value. The use case is fully tested with fakes.
detailedInstructions: Read the preamble's report shape and Technical arbitrations, and the phase-01 handoff for the domain's exact exports. Follow the `effect-services`, `infrastructure-adapters` and `validation-boundaries` skills. No new port may be called from `src/domain/`.

Git port (`src/ports/git.ts`): add `commitBefore(repo, instant): Effect<string | null, GitError>`, implemented as `git rev-list -1 --before=<instant> HEAD` and returning null when nothing comes out. Add `blobSizes(repo, commit, paths): Effect<Readonly<Record<string, number>>, GitError>`, implemented as one `git cat-file --batch-check=%(objectsize)` fed `<commit>:<path>` lines, with a missing path giving 0. Implement both in `src/infra/git.ts`. In `src/infra/fakes/git.ts`, record the calls and let tests seed the answers.

Extract the routing security filter. Add `securityFilterFor(policy: SecurityPolicy): SecurityFilter` to `src/domain/security/capabilities.ts`. It allows every provider when `policy.mode !== "secure"`. Otherwise it allows a provider only when `evaluateProviderSecurity(provider, policy).satisfiesStrict`, and gives the same refusal reason as today. Replace the two identical inline filters in `src/app/executePlan.ts` (phase routing and compliance-review routing) with calls to it. Their behaviour must not change.
Export the existing `runFolderOf(stateRoot, entry)` from `src/app/costBackfill.ts` and `COST_LEDGERS_DIR` from `src/app/prune.ts`, with no behaviour change.

`src/app/estimateHistory.ts`: `readEstimateHistory({ stateRoot, repoRoot, namespace })` returns `{ ledgers: LedgerSource[], sizedRuns: SizedRun[], unledgeredRuns: number, skipped: { path, reason }[] }`. It requires FileSystem and Git, and fails with `FsError | RegistryCorruptionError`. For each registry entry (`readRegistry`, every namespace), take `runFolderOf`. A missing folder is ignored. A missing `cost-ledger.json` counts as unledgered. Decode the ledger through `readCostLedgerFile`; an undecodable one goes to `skipped` and is not fatal. The `runKey` is `runKey(namespace, shortName)` plus `.` plus `runId`. When `entry.namespace === namespace`, also read `phax-plan.json` through `readPhaxPlanFile` and take `commitBefore(repoRoot, entry.createdAt)` and `blobSizes` for each phase's edit and optional lists. That builds a `SizedRun` with `startedAt = entry.createdAt` and `createCount = plannedFilesToCreate.length`. A missing or undecodable plan, a null base commit or a GitError leaves the run unsized (ledger still used) and is noted in `skipped`. Then list `<stateRoot>/cost-ledgers/*.json` (an absent directory means none) and decode each as a ledger only, with `runKey` = the file name without `.json`.

`src/schemas/claudeCredentials.ts`: `{ claudeAiOauth: optional Struct({ accessToken: Schema.Redacted(Schema.NonEmptyString), expiresAt: optional NonNegative number (epoch ms) }) }`. Ignore excess properties, so the refresh token and every other key are never decoded or retained. `src/schemas/oauthUsage.ts`: the endpoint answer `{ five_hour: Window, seven_day: Window }`, where Window is `{ utilization: NonNegative number (percent), resets_at: NullOr(ISO-8601 instant with Z or ±hh:mm offset) }`. Excess properties are ignored, which covers the `limits` array and other windows. Expose a decode returning Either, and a formatter naming the failing path only (for example `without five_hour`), never the values.

`src/ports/subscriptionCredentials.ts`: tag `SubscriptionCredentials` with `read(): Effect<CredentialReading, never>`. `CredentialReading` is one of `{ kind: "oauth"; token: Redacted<string>; expiresAt: string | null }`, `{ kind: "no-subscription"; cause: "api-key" | "no-credentials" }` or `{ kind: "unreadable"; reason: string }`. `src/ports/oauthUsage.ts`: tag `OAuthUsage` with `get(token: Redacted<string>): Effect<UsageAnswer, never>`. `UsageAnswer` is `{ kind: "answered"; status: number; body: string }` or `{ kind: "unreachable"; reason: string }`.

`src/infra/subscriptionCredentials.ts`: `makeNodeSubscriptionCredentialsLayer({ platform, env, homeDir, readKeychain? })`. If `env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is non-empty, return `no-subscription`/`api-key` and read nothing. On `darwin`, call `readKeychain`. By default it is `execFileSync("security", ["find-generic-password", "-s", "Claude Code-credentials", "-w"])`. Exit 44 means not found and falls through to the file. Any other failure is `unreadable` with the exit status only. The file is `<env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? homeDir/.claude>/.credentials.json`. Absent, it gives `no-subscription`/`no-credentials`, except that a set `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` gives `unreadable` ("CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is not read"). Decode through the schema. A JSON or schema failure is `unreadable` with a fixed message ("Claude Code credentials did not decode") that never includes the content or the parse error. A store without `claudeAiOauth` is `no-subscription`/`no-credentials`. Read only: never write, refresh, print or log.

`src/infra/oauthUsage.ts`: `makeNodeOAuthUsageLayer({ fetch = globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs = 10_000 })` sends a GET to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with `Authorization: Bearer <Redacted.value(token)>`, `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` and `Accept: application/json`, under `AbortSignal.timeout`. It returns `answered` with the status and body text. A thrown error becomes `unreachable`, with a reason built from the error's name and code only. Fakes: `src/infra/fakes/subscriptionCredentials.ts` and `src/infra/fakes/oauthUsage.ts`, configurable, counting calls and recording the tokens they received for assertions. Export both from `src/infra/fakes/index.ts`.

`src/app/subscriptionWindows.ts`: `readSubscriptionWindows(nowIso)` returns a `WindowsReading`, with requirements `SubscriptionCredentials | OAuthUsage` and no error. `no-subscription` maps to `{ kind: "no-subscription" }`. `unreadable` maps to unavailable with its reason. An `expiresAt` at or before now maps to unavailable ("the OAuth token expired at <instant>; start Claude Code to refresh it") without calling the endpoint. Otherwise call `get`: `unreachable` gives unavailable ("OAuth usage endpoint unreachable: …"), a status other than 200 gives unavailable ("OAuth usage endpoint answered <status>"), and a body that is not JSON or fails the schema gives unavailable ("OAuth usage endpoint answered a shape phax does not decode (<path>)"), never a partial read. On success, normalize the instants to UTC. A null `resets_at` or a past reset becomes utilization 0 with reset now + 5 h or 7 d. Return `source: "oauth-usage"` with `observedAt = nowIso`. Never put the token in a reason.

`src/app/estimatePlan.ts`: `estimatePlanCost({ planMdPath, repoRelPath, config, nowIso, probe })` returns an `EstimateReport`. It requires `FileSystem | Git | SubscriptionCredentials | OAuthUsage`, with no Backend and no Shell. Read the plan text. When `classifyArtifactPath(repoRelPath)` is not null, run `validateArtifact` and fail with its `ArtifactValidationError` (exit 12). Then run `extractPlanDeterministic` and `finalizeExtractedPlan`. If either fails, fail with a typed error that `exitCodeForError` maps to 1 and whose message names `phax plans lint`. Reuse an existing domain error when one fits, else add one to `src/domain/errors.ts`. Size each phase's planned files with `fs.apparentSize(join(repoRoot, path))`: edit bytes, optional bytes and the create count.

estimatePlan.ts routing: load `loadModelRouting()` and `loadProviderConfig()`. Build `resolveSecurityPolicy({ mode: config.security.profile, worktreePath: config.repoRoot, config: config.security })` and `securityFilterFor(policy)`, and run `resolveModel({ model, effort })` per phase. That gives the phase's `provider` and its `model`, the selected concrete model. For the compliance review: `disabled` unless `config.complianceReview.enabled`; otherwise resolve its model and effort the way `executePlan` routes the review, which gives `claude-code` or `other-provider`. Windows: with `probe`, call `readSubscriptionWindows(nowIso)`. Without it, call `lastObservedWindows(ledgers, nowMs)` and never touch either new port. Then call the domain's `estimatePlan` with the history from `readEstimateHistory({ stateRoot: config.stateRoot, repoRoot: config.repoRoot, namespace: config.namespace })`. Put `skipped` entries in the report's warnings by path, without content.

Tests use the fake FileSystem/Git/credentials/endpoint, temp directories for the adapters, and made-up data. Nothing reads `~/.phax`, `~/.claude` or the Keychain, and nothing calls the network. The OAuth adapter is tested with an injected `fetch`, and the credentials adapter with `platform: "linux"` and a temp home, or `darwin` with an injected `readKeychain`.
phases.boundaryContracts: Producer: the `SubscriptionCredentials` and `OAuthUsage` ports, consumed only by `src/app/subscriptionWindows.ts`. The Redacted token flows from the credentials adapter through app into the endpoint adapter, and no other code reads it. Producer: `estimatePlanCost` in `src/app/estimatePlan.ts`. Its consumer is the phase-03 CLI command, which provides `makeRepoRootedFileSystemLayer(config)`, `makeNodeGitLayer()`, `makeNodeSubscriptionCredentialsLayer({ platform: process.platform, env: process.env, homeDir: homedir() })` and `makeNodeOAuthUsageLayer()`, and renders or prints the returned `EstimateReport`. The use case's errors are `FsError | ConfigValidationError | ArtifactValidationError | RegistryCorruptionError` plus the unreadable-plan error, all mapped by `exitCodeForError`. Consumed from phase-01: `estimatePlan`, `lastObservedWindows` and the input types in `src/domain/cost/`. Shared with `phax run`: `securityFilterFor` in `src/domain/security/capabilities.ts`.
phases.testStrategy: Write the schema unit tests and the use-case integration tests first. `tests/unit/schemas/oauthUsage.test.ts`: decodes the flat keys with and without an extra `limits` array, a null `resets_at` and an offset instant. Refuses an answer without `five_hour`, with a path-only message. `tests/unit/schemas/claudeCredentials.test.ts`: the token decodes to Redacted, so `String()` and `JSON.stringify` never show it, and the refresh token is not retained. `tests/integration/subscriptionCredentials.test.ts` (temp home): API key set means no read; absent store means no-subscription; malformed file means unreadable without the sentinel token; darwin with keychain not found falls through to the file; another keychain failure means unreadable. The credentials file is byte-identical, with the same mtime, after a read (§8 token stays secret). `tests/integration/oauthUsage.test.ts`: the injected fetch receives the bearer and beta headers, a timeout gives unreachable, and the reason never contains the token. `tests/integration/gitBlobSizes.test.ts` uses `tests/helpers/tempGit.ts`: the sizes at an older commit, 0 for a missing path, and `commitBefore` before the first commit giving null. `tests/integration/estimateHistory.test.ts` (fake fs and git): kept active and archived runs, a pruned copy, an unledgered run, an undecodable ledger skipped, another namespace's run ledger-only, and an unsized run when the base commit is null. `tests/integration/subscriptionWindows.test.ts`: 15 % and 29 % give `oauth-usage` with both instants (§8 OAuth endpoint), 401, a shape without `five_hour`, unreachable, expired with no endpoint call, no-subscription, and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. `tests/integration/estimatePlan.test.ts`: an Approved plan never extracted is estimated with no Backend in the layer (§8 no model reads the plan). An off-grammar `docs/plans/` name fails with `ArtifactValidationError` (§8 exit codes). `--no-probe` makes zero calls to either port and reports `last-sample` with a stated age. A codex-routed phase is listed as `other-provider`. A sentinel token is absent from the serialized report on every windows path (§8 token stays secret). The existing executePlan and capabilities tests keep passing, and `securityFilterFor` gets a unit case in `tests/unit/security/capabilities.test.ts`.
implementationOrder: Git `commitBefore` and `blobSizes` in the port, the adapter and the fake, with their integration test.
`securityFilterFor`, then `executePlan` using it; exports from costBackfill and prune.
Schemas, ports, adapters and fakes for credentials and the OAuth usage endpoint, with their tests.
excludedScope: The CLI command, text rendering, cliDocs, the phase guard, generated usage and CLI reference files, docs, README and NEXT_STEPS: phase-03.
Refreshing or writing the OAuth token, and reading `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
Keeping more than the ledger through prune, and any cost-ledger format change.
A generic HTTP port: the OAuth usage port is deliberately narrow.
phases.expectedHandoff: Give the exact signatures and module paths of `estimatePlanCost` (`src/app/estimatePlan.ts`), its error union and the exit code each error maps to; the node layer factories and their options (`makeNodeSubscriptionCredentialsLayer`, `makeNodeOAuthUsageLayer`); the fakes' names; the new Git methods; and `securityFilterFor`. Name the typed error for an unparseable plan. Confirm that executePlan's routing behaviour is unchanged. Explain any deviation from the planned file lists.

commit.subject: feat(plans): add phax plans estimate
commit.body:
phax plans estimate <plan> reports a plan's API-list cost per phase and per run as P10/P50/P90 from this machine's cost ledgers, and whether it fits the subscription windows left now: fits, risky or wait, or why it cannot say. --json prints the report, and --no-probe uses the last rate-limit sample instead of the OAuth usage endpoint. The command exits 0 whatever the verdict and 12 for a plan that fails artifact validation. Its layer holds no Backend, so no model is ever invoked.

Inside a phase worktree the phase guard refuses the command. The usage spec, completions, CLI reference and README carry the command. docs/plan-estimate.md explains it for an operator on a Max subscription, the docs site lists it, and NEXT_STEPS ticks plan-estimate.

phases.title: phax plans estimate, its rendering and its docs
phases.objective: An operator runs `phax plans estimate <plan>`, with `--json` or `--no-probe`, and sees §6's report: the phase table, the run line, what is not estimated, the subscription windows with their calibrated capacity, the P50 and P90 scenarios, and the verdict. The command exits 0 whatever the verdict and 12 on artifact validation. The docs page, README, generated CLI files and NEXT_STEPS describe it.
detailedInstructions: Read the phase-02 handoff for `estimatePlanCost`, its errors and the node layer factories, and the preamble's report shape. Follow the `cli-view-layer` skill: the command file parses arguments, calls the one use case and renders through the OutputPort. It holds no business logic.

`src/domain/cost/estimateRender.ts`: `renderEstimate(report, { timeZone, nowMs })` returns the §6 text, which is indicative in layout. The first line is `History: <n> phases, sized by planned-file bytes, recent runs weighted (half-life 30d)`, followed by a hint to run `phax cost backfill` when `unledgeredRuns > 0`. Then comes a table with columns phase, model, effort, P10, P50 and P90, using 2 decimals. Then a `run-level  compliance review` row when `runLevel > 0`, a `run  API-list $` row, and one `Not estimated:` line naming the not-estimated phases with their reason, then the fixed invocations. Next a `Subscription (OAuth usage):` block, or `(last sample, <N> min old — usage since then is not counted)`, with one line per window: `<n>% used, resets <Fri 16 Oct 14:50>   ≈ $<capacity>/window, $<left> left`, or `not calibrated`. Then the `P50:` and `P90:` scenario lines (`fits — agent time ends ≈ HH:MM`, or each pause: `<window> exhausted in <phase> ≈ HH:MM, resumes HH:MM`). The last line is `Verdict: <verdict> — <one-line explanation>`.

Render the other cases as follows. Thin history prints `History: <n> phases — an estimate needs 60; none printed` and the verdict, with no table. Windows unavailable prints `Subscription: windows unavailable — <reason>` and `Verdict: windows-unavailable — estimate only`. No subscription prints `Verdict: no-subscription — estimate only`. Uncalibrated names the windows, or the burn rate, that lacked samples. Format instants with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the given `timeZone` (weekday, day, month, 24-hour time). The renderer is pure and takes `nowMs` only to compute the sample's age.

`src/cli/commands/plansEstimate.ts`: `runPlansEstimate(plan, { json?: true, noProbe?: true }, out)`. Load the config with `loadConfig(process.cwd())`; a config error exits 1. Absolutize and compute `repoRelPath` exactly as `runPlansLint` does. Provide `Layer.mergeAll(makeRepoRootedFileSystemLayer(config), makeNodeGitLayer(), makeNodeSubscriptionCredentialsLayer({ platform: process.platform, env: process.env, homeDir: homedir() }), makeNodeOAuthUsageLayer())`, with no Backend and no Shell, and run `estimatePlanCost({ …, nowIso: new Date().toISOString(), probe: !noProbe })`. An error is printed with `out.error` and exits with `exitCodeForError`, which gives 12 for artifact validation. On success, `--json` writes `JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)` to stdout, and warnings go through `out.warn` so stdout stays one document. Otherwise it writes `renderEstimate(report, { timeZone: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone, nowMs: Date.now() })`. It always exits 0 after a report (§5.15).

Register the command in `src/cli/commands/plans.ts`, next to `lint`, as `plansCmd.command("estimate")` with argument `<plan>` ("Path to the plan.md"), `--json` ("Emit the estimate as JSON") and `--no-probe` ("Use the last rate-limit sample in the cost ledgers instead of the OAuth usage endpoint"). Commander reports `--no-probe` as `opts.probe === false`. The description is: "Estimate a plan's API-list cost and whether it fits the subscription windows now". Update the `plans` group description to mention estimating.

Add `plans estimate` to `src/cli/cliDocs.ts`. Its summary is the description above. The long help names the history (cost ledgers, at least 60 sized phases of this repository, weighted with a half-life of 30 days), the windows source (the OAuth usage endpoint reading Claude Code's OAuth token from the macOS Keychain or `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, never writing or refreshing it; `--no-probe` for the last sample), the verdict values and what is never estimated. The examples are the §11 commands, with made-up plan paths. The exit codes are 0 (any verdict), 1 (config error, or a plan the deterministic parser cannot read) and 12 (artifact validation). Classify `"plans estimate": "refused"` in `src/domain/security/phaseGuard.ts`.

Run `pnpm gen:usage-spec` and `pnpm docs:cli`. Never hand-edit `phax.usage.kdl`, `docs/cli/reference.md` or the README's generated CLI section. If the completions or usage-spec tests need a fixture update for the new command, update it.

`docs/plan-estimate.md` (§11). The reader is an operator on a Claude Max subscription deciding whether to start a run now or after the next window reset, and what it will cost. Start with the §11 example block (`phax cost backfill`, then `phax plans estimate docs/plans/<stamp>-<slug>-plan.md`, then the `--no-probe --json | jq .verdict` form). Then explain: where the history comes from and why `phax cost backfill` comes first; the 60-phase minimum; reading the table (P10/P50/P90, API-list dollars, not what the subscription bills); how windows are read (the OAuth usage endpoint is undocumented, the token is read and never written, macOS may ask once for Keychain access, and API-key users get `no-subscription`); `--no-probe` and its staleness; capacity recalibrated from the last 28 days; every verdict value and what to do about it; what is not estimated (plan extraction, plan auditor, interactive code review, Codex and Vibe phases); and the exit codes. Use only made-up numbers; §6's may be reused.
Add a `files` entry to `site/pages.ts` for `docs/plan-estimate.md`: route `/guide/plan-estimate`, title `Estimating a plan`, and a one-sentence description. Place it with the other guide pages.

README, by hand: in the plans command list next to `phax plans lint`, add `phax plans estimate <plan>` with a one-line comment, and link `docs/plan-estimate.md` where the README lists docs pages. NEXT_STEPS.md: tick `plan-estimate` and drop its `**Next.**`.
Tests never spawn a provider, never call the network, never read `~/.phax`, `~/.claude` or the Keychain.
phases.boundaryContracts: Consumer: `src/cli/commands/plansEstimate.ts` consumes `estimatePlanCost` from `src/app/estimatePlan.ts` and the node layers from `src/infra/subscriptionCredentials.ts`, `src/infra/oauthUsage.ts`, `src/infra/git.ts` and the repo-rooted FileSystem. It only chooses between `JSON.stringify(report)` and `renderEstimate(report, …)` and maps errors to exit codes. Producer: `renderEstimate` in `src/domain/cost/estimateRender.ts`, which reads `EstimateReport` only. The `--json` field names and verdict values are the ones §6 makes normative, plus the variants Q1 decided.
phases.testStrategy: Write `tests/unit/cost/estimateRender.test.ts` first, rendering made-up reports with `timeZone: "UTC"`: the §6 risky layout (table, run-level row, run row, Not estimated line, both windows with capacity and dollars left, P50 fits and P90 pause lines, the Verdict line), thin history (no table, names 12 phases), windows unavailable naming the 401, no-subscription, uncalibrated, a last-sample age line, and an `other-provider` phase in the Not estimated line. `tests/integration/plansEstimateCommand.test.ts` spawns `tsx src/cli/main.ts` as `tests/integration/phaseGuard.test.ts` does. It uses its own temp git repo with a `phax.json` whose `state.root` is inside the temp dir, with `HOME` set to a temp dir, and with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` removed from the inherited environment. Every invocation passes either `--no-probe` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=test-not-a-key`, so no credential store is read. Cases: a `docs/plans/` plan with an off-grammar name exits 12. A valid plan with no history exits 0 and names 0 phases, with `--no-probe --json` giving a single JSON document whose verdict is `thin-history`. The same plan without `--no-probe` and with the dummy API key also exits 0 (§5.15). Inside a phase worktree, the phase guard refuses the command (unit classification test). The usage-spec drift, lint, examples and completions tests confirm that the generated files are in step.
implementationOrder: `plansEstimate.ts`, its registration in `plans.ts`, and its integration test.
cliDocs and the phase guard, then `pnpm gen:usage-spec` and `pnpm docs:cli`.
excludedScope: Gating `phax run` on the verdict, or showing the estimate at run start (spec §7).
Scheduling or delaying a run until a reset.
Estimating plan extraction, the plan auditor, the interactive code review, or Codex and Vibe phases and their quotas.
Any change to the domain model, adapters or history reader beyond what rendering needs.
phases.verification: The `standard` gate profile in `phax.json`, including its terminal `pnpm build`, `pnpm site:build` and smoke steps.
phases.expectedHandoff: Show the final text and JSON output for a made-up risky report and for thin history, list the cliDocs entry and the phase-guard classification, and confirm that the generated files were regenerated, not hand-edited. Give the docs route and the README and NEXT_STEPS edits. Explain any deviation from the planned file lists, including any test fixtures touched for completions or usage-spec drift.
